This note looks at the participation of Lok Sabha MPs during the 17th Lok Sabha. MPs who are ministers, and the Speaker do not ask questions or introduce private member bills. Women in Parliament and State Assemblies
The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2023 was introduced in Lok Sabha on September 19, 2023.  The Bill seeks to reserve one-third of all seats for women in Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.  A similar Bill had been introduced in Rajya Sabha in 2008, and was passed by the House two years later.  It lapsed after the dissolution of the 14th Lok Sabha in 2014.  This note takes a look at participation of women in Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies.

About IndiaVotes
IndiaVotes is a public database of Indian election results — Lok Sabha
(the lower house of the national parliament) and Vidhan Sabha (state legislative
assemblies). Sourced from the Election Commission of India and curated for
consistency across decades of changing constituency boundaries, party splits
and mergers, and state reorganisations.
What we cover
Lok Sabha — 1952 onwards. All 18 general elections from
the first general election after independence through 2024. Per-constituency
results, candidate-level vote counts, party tallies, turnout and margin figures.
Vidhan Sabha — 1977 onwards (for most states).
State assembly results from the late 1970s through the most recent elections
in 2024-25. A handful of states start a year or two later: Andhra Pradesh
(1978), Sikkim (1979), Gujarat and Manipur (1980). State-formation cohorts
naturally start later: Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh in their current
boundaries from 2003, Jharkhand from 2005, Telangana and the post-split
Andhra Pradesh from 2014.
Earlier assembly elections (1952-1976) are not in this archive — they pre-date
the source records we work from. Filling that pre-1977 gap is on the long-term
plan.
Bye-elections — 1,245 entries across both houses, surfaced on
every constituency page and indexed at /bye-elections/.
Constituency boundary maps for the 2008 delimitation (Lok
Sabha and Vidhan Sabha). Earlier delimitations (1952-1971, 1977-2004) render
with limited geometry — that gap is also tracked on the long-term plan.
How the site works
Built as a static archive: every page is pre-rendered at build time and served
from a global content network. There's no database behind the public site —
results are checked into version control as JSON and regenerated when new
election data is published.
For attribution and the full list of upstream sources, see
/license/.

Assembly Election Results 2026 Highlights- 'Aaj Bengal bhaymukt hua hai', says PM Modi on BJP's big win
Assembly Election Results 2026 Highlights- ‘Aaj Bengal bhaymukt hua hai’, says PM Modi on BJP’s big win
Assembly Election Results 2026 Highlights | West Bengal, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Assam, Puducherry Election Results on eci.gov.in, results.eci.gov.in
Written by Sakshi Kuchroo
Updated:  May 5, 2026 06:41 IST
Addressing party workers at the party headquarters here after the results and trends showed BJP heading for a sweeping victory in West Bengal and NDA's strong wins in Assam and Puducherry, PM Modi said the result marks trust in the politics of performance.
Follow Us
Assembly Election Results 2026 Highlights: ‘The lotus has bloomed’ – Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Monday, as the BJP breached Trinamool Congress’s West Bengal fortress and is set to form a government in the state. The BJP-led NDA has also recorded victories in Assam and Puducherry.
Addressing party workers at the party headquarters here after the results and trends showed BJP heading for a sweeping victory in West Bengal and NDA’s strong wins in Assam and Puducherry, PM Modi said the result marks trust in the politics of performance.
“Today is a historic day. It is unprecedented. When years of efforts turn into success, the happiness that is seen on the faces of people is the same happiness that I see on the faces of BJP workers across the country today,” he said.
“As a party worker, I share the joy of every BJP worker. Today is a special day in many ways. It marks the announcement of a bright future for the country. This is a day of trust. Trust in India’s great democracy. Trust in the politics of performance… Trust in the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat Shrestha Bharat’,” he added.
Assembly Election Results 2026 Highlights: What’s at stake across 5 states?
This is one of the most consequential counting days Indian politics has seen in years where five legislatures are to be decided simultaneously. The results will be seen not just as state mandates but as a political temperature check ahead of the 2029 general elections.
What do latest trends say for West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Assam, Puducherry, and Kerala?
West Bengal is emerging as one of the most closely watched states in the early counting phase, with initial trends showing the Bharatiya Janata Party ahead while the ruling All India Trinamool Congress trails. Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee is also behind in her home constituency of Bhabanipur, where BJP’s Suvendu Adhikari is currently leading.
In Tamil Nadu, Chief Minister M. K. Stalin’s Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam is ahead in early trends, while actor-turned-politician Vijay and his party Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam are also showing a competitive presence.
In Puducherry, early indications suggest the NDA is hoping to retain power, with initial leads pointing in its favour.
UDF Moves Past Majority Mark in Early Kerala Counting Trends
Latest data from the Election Commission of India shows the Congress-led United Democratic Front crossing the halfway mark in Kerala after the initial round of counting.
The alliance is currently ahead in more than 78 seats in the 140-member Assembly, where 78 seats are needed to form a government. The trends suggest the UDF has taken an early lead as counting continues across the state.

M.K.Stalin on election verdict, 'We accept people's judgement'
In a notable development, Tamil Nadu's MK Stalin has reacted to what many have deemed as an embarrassing and disappointing performance from his party. In a note posted on X, MK Stalin has graciously accepted the verdict of the people.
"We bow to and accept the verdict of the people. Congratulations to the victors! In the past five years, we have created numerous projects and provided good governance to the people of Tamil Nadu. We have elevated Tamil Nadu in every way. In the electoral arena, we sought votes only by speaking of our achievements," Stalin wrote on X.
"We campaigned for votes to ensure the welfare schemes we delivered to the people would continue. I express my heartfelt thanks to all the people of Tamil Nadu who supported and voted for the secular progressive alliance led by the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam," he added.
Notably, Stalin lost from his own home constituency of Kolathur earlier today as per electoral data posted by ECI.

Assembly Election Results 2024: Steps to check Haryana, Jammu & Kashmir results online at results.eci.gov.in, eci.gov.in
Check Assembly Election Result 2024 for Haryana, J&K Election Results Live on results.eci.gov.in and eci.gov.in: The results for the Haryana elections will be announced on the Election Commission of India's official website from 8 AM onwards.
Written by India News Desk
Updated:  October 8, 2024 08:57 IST
How to Check Haryana, J&K Election Results on results.eci.gov.in.
Follow Us
How to Check Assembly Election 2024 Live Vote Counting on results.eci.gov.in: As the Haryana and Jammu and Kashmir Assembly results will be out today voters and political enthusiasts alike are eager to stay informed about the results of the northern state and the Union Territory. The Election Commission of India (ECI) serves as the official source for election results, providing real-time updates on latest trends and winning and trailing candidates.
To find the election results for both Haryana and Jammu and Kashmir, visit the ECI website at eci.gov.in. Once on the homepage, navigate to the “Election Results” section, which can found in the main menu. Here, you will find links to the latest results from various states, including the Haryana and Jammu and Kashmir elections.

On the results page, you can access detailed information about each constituency, including the number of votes cast, leading candidates, and the final tallies for each party. The ECI website also features a user-friendly interface that allows you to search for specific constituencies or candidates, making it easier to find the information you need.
You can access the result for Jammu and Kashmir and Haryana here on the official ECI website here: https://results.eci.gov.in/. The results trends will start from 8:00AM on 8 October, 2024 on the official website of the ECI.

This way, you can stay informed about the political landscape in Haryana and Jammu and Kashmir as it unfolds.
